messages.author: Norbert Kopco
messages.title: Kosice Neuroscience Workshop, 19 - 21 April, 2027
messages.body_html:
SAVE THE DATE

The 6th workshop on

Cognitive neuroscience of auditory and cross-modal perception

19 - 21 April 2027, Košice (pronounced KOH-shih-tse), Slovakia
https://pcl.upjs.sk/workshop-2024

Objectives:

  • The workshop centers on how people perceive, attend to, and understand sounds—especially speech—in complex spatial, noisy, multimodal, and technologically mediated environments.
  • It aims to connect basic auditory mechanisms with real-world listening applications, using innovative tools such as games, mobile measures, neuroimaging, modeling, virtual environments, and hearing technologies. 
  • It will include advanced research talks (and introductory lectures) on a range of topics related to the neural processes of auditory, visual and cross-modal perception.
  • The workshop is aimed at early-stage and advanced students and young researchers, and it will provide ample opportunities for direct interactions between the lecturers and the attendees.

The workshop will follow up on our previous workshops. 

Guest speakers and SAV consortium speakers (tentative)

Inyong Choi, University of Iowa, United States
Norbert Vanek, University of Auckland, New Zealand
Eleni Vlahou, University of Thessaly, Greece
Mathieu Lavandier, ENTPE - University of Lyon France
Robert Baumgartner, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria
Piotr Majdak, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria
Anja Pahor, Univerza v Mariboru, Slovenia
Jyrki Ahveninen, Mass General Research Institute / Harvard Medical School, United States
Virginia Best; Boston University, United States
Aaron Seitz, Northeastern University, United States
Norbert Kopco, P. J. Šafárik University in Košice, Slovakia

Registration:

The workshop is open to all interested students/scientists. Registration is free of charge but required. To register, please send an email to EMAIL_REDACTED stating your full name and affiliation and the dates on which you are planning to attend. All accepted abstracts will be published on the workshop website and in the abstract book. No proceedings will be published. In case you would like to have a presentation please send us an abstract (up to 200 words; also indicate whether you prefer poster or oral presentation) no later than February 1, 2027. Also, see travel grant info below.

Student travel grants:

We offer a limited number of travel awards of 250 EUR to offset the cost of attending for students and young researcher. To apply, you need to be a presenting author. Please also introduce yourself and describe your motivation / reasons you need the travel grant.

Organizers:

Norbert Kopco, P. J. Šafárik University in Košice
Eleni Vlahou, University of Thessaly
Frederick Gallun, Oregon Health and Science University
Robert Baumgartner, Austrian Academy of Sciences
Piotr Majdak, Austrian Academy of Sciences
Mathieu Lavandier, ENTPE – University of Lyon
Aaron Seitz, Northeastern University
Perception and Cognition Lab

Acknowledgement:

The project has received funding from the HORIZON-MSCA-2022-SE-01 call (MSCA Staff Exchanges) of the research and innovation programme of Horizon Europe under the Marie Sklodowska-Curie actions grant agreement N° 101129903.

Sponsorship:

Organization of the workshop has been partially supported by the European Acoustics Association.

messages.author: I-Chun Lin
messages.title: GCNU-SWC Joint PhD Programme: Applications now open!
messages.body_html:
Gatsby Unit and Sainsbury Wellcome Centre Joint PhD Programme

Deadline: 17:00 GMT, Monday 9 November 2026

This four-year joint PhD programme, launched by the Gatsby Computational Neuroscience Unit (GCNU) and Sainsbury Wellcome Centre for Neural Circuits and Behaviour (SWC), aims to bridge the gap between theory and experiment. The programme immerses students in both experimental and theoretical thinking, providing rigorous training in a supportive environment for an interdisciplinary research career in academia or industry. First-year courses provide a comprehensive introduction to systems neuroscience, theoretical/computational neuroscience and machine learning. Students will be part of a broader trainee cohort across both centres, interacting and engaging in scientific discussion with both SWC and GCNU researchers with equal emphasis.

GCNU and SWC provide a unique opportunity to bring together a critical mass of theoreticians and experimentalists, fostering close interaction both among themselves and with researchers in the ELLIS Unit at UCL and across related UCL departments and domains, such as UCL Neuroscience Domain; Artificial Intelligence; Computer Science; Statistical Science; as well as researchers at the nearby Francis Crick Institute.

The applicants should have a strong analytical and mathematical background, a keen interest in neuroscience, and a relevant first degree (e.g., in Computer Science, Cognitive Psychology, Engineering, Mathematics, Neuroscience, Physics, Statistics).

Full funding is available regardless of nationality. We also welcome applicants who have secured, or are seeking, funding from other sources.

More information on the joint programme (including the key differences between the three PhD programmes offered by GCNU and SWC) and details on how to apply can be found on https://www.ucl.ac.uk/life-sciences/gatsby/study-and-work/gcnu-swc-joint-phd-programme.

--
I-Chun Lin, PhD
Scientific Programme Manager
Gatsby Computational Neuroscience Unit, UCL

messages.title: Reminder – Register for NeuralNet 2026! ￼ ￼
messages.body_html:
Dear colleagues,

A quick reminder that registration for NeuralNet 2026 is still open!

Join us in Paris on November 25–27 at the Odéon Campus of Université Paris Cité for three days of exciting science, discussion, and networking across Systems and Computational Neuroscience.

There are still a few talk slots available, and we warmly welcome abstract submissions for both talks and posters. So, if you haven't registered yet, now is a great time to do so!

👉 More information & registration

We look forward to welcoming you to Paris in November!

Best regards,
The NeuralNet 2026 Organizing Committee
